channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Deloitte UK Partner Pay Grows to $1.5 Million on AI Demand
item.description: Deloitte’s UK business paid its equity partners an average of about £1.13 million ($1.5 million) last year, up 7% from the year prior as the firm said demand for advice on artificial intelligence drove profit.
item.dc:creator: James Booth

item.title: BMO US Commercial Bank Head on Yields, M&A Pipeline
item.description: Tony Sciarrino, BMO's US Commercial Bank Head, said rising interest rates have not yet caused a meaningful slowdown in client planning or borrowing. He said BMO’s client roundtables show companies remain focused on growth, even though executing in a higher-rate environment requires more discipline and stronger performance than when rates were lower. He speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Responds to AI Backlash With ‘Super Intelligence’ Rebrand
item.description: President Donald Trump sees artificial intelligence as suffering from a branding problem, and he intends to fix it with an attempt to officially rename the technology “super intelligence.”
item.dc:creator: Michael Shepard

item.title: Altman on OpenAI's IPO Plans, AI Agent Dots, AI Security
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman talks about launching its new AI personal agent called Dots, which he says is a premium product. Altman also says the company will go public at some point, but it's being patient. He speaks to Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow in San Francisco. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloom CEO Says Growth Goals Intact Despite AI Slowdown Concerns
item.description: Bloom Energy Corp. Chief Executive Officer KR Sridhar says he’s confident that “speed bumps” in the buildout of artificial-intelligence infrastructure won’t hurt the company’s growth plans.
item.dc:creator: Emma Haidar

item.title: Bloom Energy CEO: Power Demand Is Coming From All Angles
item.description: Bloom Energy marked its 25th anniversary by ringing the New York Stock Exchange opening bell, just days after joining the S&P 500, and used the moment to highlight its role in powering AI infrastructure. CEO K.R. Sridhar said Bloom’s on-site power systems are becoming a standard solution as demand rises for data centers, factories, and hospitals. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MongoDB Not in a Rush to Find CEO Successor, Ittycheria Says
item.description: MongoDB Interim President and CEO Dev Ittycheria discusses the outlook for the company after Meta Platforms tapped former CEO Chirantan “CJ” Desai to lead a new AI platform for enterprise customers. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Accelevation IPO Prices Below Range to Raise $540 Million
item.description: Accelevation Holdings Corp., a data center infrastructure company, and backer Olympus Partners raised $540 million in a US initial public offering priced below its marketed range, after a handful of first-time share sales were postponed.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz and Anthony Hughes

item.title: Trump Rejects AI Safety Laws After Meeting Industry Titans
item.description: President Donald Trump shot down the idea of new federal regulations on AI after meeting at the White House with top industry executives amid growing global concerns over threats posed by the technology. Tyler Kendall has more (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI CFO Friar on New AI Assistant, Capital Raise
item.description: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar discusses the company's new proactive assistant Dots. Speaking with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg The Close," Friar also says OpenAI is "really well capitalized." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Future of Derivatives Markets Being Laid: Shahrawat
item.description:
D. Shahrawat with Bloomberg Intelligence joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss new regulations being made after the Clarity Act failed, and how top trading platforms are facing disruption in their industry. They also preview the upcoming Bloomberg Intelligence Derivatives Market Structure conference being held in New York City on Sept. 30, 2026.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: David Fincher to End Deal With Netflix, Adding to String of Departures
item.description: Fincher has worked at Netflix for longer than just about any creative, starting as a director and executive producer of the service’s landmark original series House of Cards.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Shaw

item.title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI Investors Patient With IPO Plan
item.description: CEO Sam Altman says OpenAI ultimately wants to become a public company, but not yet. Speaking with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg The Close," Altman pushes back on the idea that the responsibilities of being public are incompatible with a focus on safety. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Altman Says OpenAI Investors Patient on IPO Amid Safety Focus
item.description: OpenAI’s Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said the company wants to navigate a period of heightened artificial intelligence safety concerns without the pressure of being a newly public company and believes investors will be “patient” with its IPO planning.
item.dc:creator: Seth Fiegerman and Ed Ludlow

item.title: OpenAI Will Keep Driving Down AI Prices, Sam Altman Says
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the company wants to drive up the quality of AI while keeping the price down. He talks about the launch of their new AI agent called Dots with Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow at the company's annual developer conference in San Francisco. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
item.description: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent weeks, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.
item.dc:creator: William Norris, Nilushi Karunaratne and Thomas Pfeiffer

item.title: Trump Hosts AI Leaders at White House
item.description: Artificial intelligence industry leaders met with President Donald Trump to discuss growing concerns over threats posed by the technology. Trump has said he doesn't want to stifle innovation by using too much regulation. Palantir Technologies CEO Alex Karp was among those at the meeting and he spoke to Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Citi, Coinbase Team Up To Let Merchants Accept Stablecoins
item.description: Bloomberg's Anna Irrera joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Citigroup is partnering with Coinbase Global to allow the bank’s institutional clients to accept stablecoin payments, as large financial institutions step up their involvement in new forms of digital money. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Targets $30 Billion in Funding at $1.4 Trillion Value
item.description: OpenAI aims to raise at least $30 billion from investors in a new round of funding, according to people familiar with the matter, after the artificial intelligence startup pushed back its plans for an initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence, Ed Ludlow and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Anthropic Flags ‘Catastrophic’ Risks in IPO Filing: Reuters
item.description: Anthropic PBC warned that its technology poses “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” and mapped out plans to spend hundreds of billions of dollars in its prospectus as the artificial intelligence company prepared for its initial public offering, Reuters reported.
item.dc:creator: Amy Thomson
